name: Archaeological Site of Aigai (modern name Vergina)
description: Aigai, today's Vergina in northern Greece, was the first capital of ancient Macedonia, set on the foothills above a broad plain. Visitors can see the ruins of a vast palace once decked with mosaics and painted stucco, and a burial ground of over 300 mounds, the oldest dating to the 11th century B.C. Beneath the Great Tumulus lies a royal tomb identified as that of Philip II, father of Alexander the Great.
